previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD, CABG, COPD, esophagitis, and alcohol abuse was admitted for chest pain that occurred while attempting to eat spinach, which he felt stuck in his throat, followed by vomiting and chest pressure. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal troponins and non-diagnostic EKG changes. A CT abdomen showed no acute surgical process but noted a stable moderate-to-severe SMA stenosis and a hiatal hernia. An EGD revealed severe esophageal ulceration and a 9 mm stricture at the gastroesophageal junction, which was dilated to 12 mm. His chest pain was attributed to esophageal pathology rather than cardiac causes. He was managed with acid suppression, including a switch from omeprazole to sublingual lansoprazole for better compliance, and a soft diet. He remained stable, with no arrhythmias or respiratory deterioration, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient EGD follow-up and continued medication management.

# N/V/chest and abd pain: One week after esophageal stricture 
dilatation in patient with continued EtOH abuse and history of 
ulcerative esophagitis.  The exam was concerning for 
mediasteinitis with CT scan confirming esophagitis and 
mediasteinitis. This was supported by lactate, leukocytosis and 
low grade fever. There was concern for microperforation even 
with negative CT scan. He had an upper GI series (esophagus 
fluoroscopy) that showed no evidence of esophageal perforation, 
however there was still some worry that there could have been a 
microperforation that was not observed radiographically. An EGD 
was not done given the risk of perforation. Blood cultures were 
drawn, and he was started on ceftriaxone and flagyl to cover for 
translocation (10 day course). He was kept NPO, and was started 
on TPN for nutritional support. He has since been strictly NPO 
with TPN for a week to try and decrease the inflammation 
surrounding the esophagus. He was reimaged to reevaluate his 
esophagus, and CT ___ showed marked interval improvement in 
degree of esophageal wall thickening and periesophageal fat 
stranding, consistent with improving esophagitis. He was put on 
a sips trial which he successfully passed. He has done well so 
far and continues with sips of light clear fluids, but will 
remain on TPN until he is able to take in all of his nutritional 
support.  GI did NOT want any PO medications until he follows up 
in outpatient GI clinic, and all medications were given by IV 
form.
 
# Hematemesis:  Likely related to underlying esophagitis, but 
___ tear was also a possibility. He had guiac positive 
stools, which later resolved. 

# PAF: Reported self limited atrial flutter in the ED, resolved 
after IVF.  He received no anticoagulation given the risk of 
bleeding. He was followed on telemetry, his home diltiazem was 
held and was covered with IV metoprolol. He was taken off of 
metoprolol as HR was <100 without need for rate control.  He was 
discharged off all nodal agents.
 
# H/o CAD s/p CABG & Stable angina:  Stable.
  
# COPD: chronic dyspnea observed on exam.  No wheezing, no 
further hypoxia. We continued O2 supplement, as well as his home 
tiotropium, fluticasone, and albuterol.
  
# Normocytic Anemia:  Anemia of chronic disease based on iron 
studies in ___, plus acute blood loss from hematemesis. His 
HCT has been stable during his hospitalization.  

# H/o alcohol abuse: Serum tox screen negative despite his 
report of having beer the day of coming to the ED. We continued 
folic acid, thiamine, and MVI via banana bag. The CIWA scale was 
ordered with ativan IV q4h prn. 
  
# Hypothyroidism: Pt was continued on home levothyroxine via IV 
form.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with history of cirrhosis, presents with fever
and vomiting as well as chest pain.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the pubic
symphysis following administration of intravenous, without oral contrast due
to intolerance.  Multiplanar reformations were generated.

CT CHEST:  There is no evidence of pneumomediastinum.  Note is made of
circumferential mural thickening and mucosal hyperemia along the mid-to-lower
esophagus extending to the level fo the gastroesophageal junction, with mild
surrounding inflammation.  There is increase in mediastinal lymphadenopathy in
the paratracheal, pretracheal, precarinal, and subcarinal location up to 13
mm, likely reactive.  

There is no axillary adenopathy.  Although not tailored for evaluation of
pulmonary embolism, there are no large central filling defects to suggest
pulmonary embolism.  There is biapical pulmonary scarring.  Patchy right upper
lobe reticular opacity slight more prominent since ___, nonspecific. 
Predominantly right-sided paraseptal emphysematous changes are present.  There
are trace left greater than right effusions.  Bibasilar dependent atelectasis
is noted.  Central airways remain patent.

The heart is normal in size without pericardial effusion.  Multivessel
coronary arterial and aortic valve calcifications are noted.

CT ABDOMEN:  The liver appears mildly lobulated without definite focal lesion.
The gallbladder contains a stone without evidence of cholecystitis.  The
spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable.  The pancreas appears diffusely
atrophic.  Bilateral kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis or
hydroureter, containing multiple cysts, some of which are too small to fully
characterize, the largest cyst measuring 2.8 cm on the right.  There is a
small axial hiatal hernia.  Small and large bowel loops are normal in caliber.
There is no evidence of obstruction.  No free air or free fluid.  Scattered
diverticulosis of the colon is seen without diverticulitis.  No mesenteric
adenopathy.

Great vessels are patent although moderate atherosclerotic calcifications are
seen involving the descending aorta with extension into left greater than
right renal arteries and celiac trunk and SMA.

CT PELVIS:  The bladder is massively distended and decompression should be
considered.  The rectum and prostate appear within normal limits.  No pelvic
sidewall or inguinal adenopathy.  No free fluid in the pelvis.

BONE WINDOW:  No focal concerning lesion.  Moderate multilevel thoracolumbar
spondylosis, disc space narrowing, and endplate sclerosis is present.  The
patient is status post median sternotomy.  Minimal retrolisthesis is present
at L5-S1.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Circumferential esophageal wall thickening and hyperemia of mid-to-lower
esophagus extending to the GE junction with paraesophageal stranding,
consistent with esophagitis.   Increased mediastinal stranding and adenopathy
suggest mediastinitis.  No pneumomediastinum to indicate frank perforation,
though microperforation cannot be excluded.  History of recent endoscopy and
dilation was obtained later. 

2.  No bowel obstruction.

3.  Cholelithiasis.

4.  Trace left pleural effusion.  Right predominant emphysema.

5.  Renal cysts.

6.  Trace pleural effusions, new on the left since ___.

Findings reported to Dr. ___ via phone at 8:30 a.m. on ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with ulcerative esophagitis with nausea,
vomiting, and chest pain and esophageal inflammation on CT.  Evaluate for
perforation.

COMPARISON:  CT ___.  The report from endoscopies ___ and ___
were reviewed in the ___ medical record.  

SINGLE CONTRAST ESOPHAGRAM: Spot fluoroscopic images were obtained while
patient is ingesting Optiray.  Contrast passes freely through the esophagus
without evidence of hold up.  No leak is detected to suggest esophageal
perforation.  No large stricture is identified.  The stomach empties promptly
and is grossly unremarkable.  Again noted is a fractured superior most median
sternotomy wire as seen on chest radiograph ___.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of esophageal perforation.

HISTORY:  New right PICC line.

CHEST, SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW.

A right subclavian PICC line is present.  The tip overlies the right IJ vein
at the level of the mid cervical spine.  No pneumothorax is detected.  

This finding was discussed by radiology resident, M. ___, with ___
___, IV nurse, by phone at 7:20 p.m. on ___.  Please see detailed wet

HISTORY:  Malpositioned right PICC tip termination post-power flush.

CHEST, SINGLE AP VIEW.

A right subclavian PICC line is present.  The tip extends cephalad and
overlies the right neck, extending beyond the upper edge of this film, likely
following the right internal jugular vein. No pneumothorax is detected. This
finding was discussed by radiology resident, M. ___, with IV nurse, ___
___, at 8:15 p.m. on ___, as detailed in the wet reading.  

Again seen is hyperinflation, sternotomy wires, prominence  of
cardiomediastinal silhouette, patchy bibasilar opacities, and small bilateral
effusions, with residual contrast in the splenic flexure.  There is mild upper
zone prominence, without overt CHF.  The two upper sternal wires and possibly
the fourth down-from-top sternal wire are interrupted.    

IMPRESSION:  Right subclavian PICC line malpositioned, coursing cephalad along
the right internal jugular vein, beyond the edge of this film.

PICC REPLACEMENT

INDICATION:  ___ man with severe esophagitis and mediastinitis who
requires TPN.  Need to advance the midline PICC line into the central
position.

OPERATORS:  ___, M.D.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  The procedure was explained to the patient.  The
patient was brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
angiographic table.  The existing PICC line in the right arm was prepped and
draped in usual sterile fashion.  Initial scout fluoroscopic images
demonstrated the tip of the PICC line in the right axillary vein.  The
existing PICC line was cut and a nitinol wire was placed through and navigated
into the SVC.  The old PICC line was removed.  A peel-away sheath was placed
over the wire.  Through the peel-away sheath, a new double lumen Power PICC
line measuring 38.5 cm length was then placed.  The wire and the peel-away
sheath were removed.  The distal tip of the PICC line is in the distal SVC. 
Both lumens flushed easily.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well.  No immediate post-procedure complications were
noted.

IMPRESSION:  Successful replacement of the existing PICC line.  Currently, the
distal tip of the PICC line is in distal SVC.  The final length of the PICC
line is 38.5 cm.  The catheter is ready to use.

INDICATION:  Esophagitis and mediastinitis one week ago, n.p.o. and on TPN for
the last week.  Evaluate for improvement in esophagitis and mediastinitis.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the chest during infusion
of 75 cc of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar reformations were
performed.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___.

FINDINGS:  Compared to prior CT from ___, there has been a
marked improvement in the degree of esophageal mural thickening extending from
its midpoint through the GE junction.  Previously seen mucosal
hyperenhancement throughout this segment has resolved and the degree of
periesophageal fat stranding has substantially decreased.  Reactive
mediastinal lymphadenopathy, measuring up to 10 mm (2:11), has slightly
decreased.  There is no free air in the mediastinum to suggest esophageal
perforation.  There is a new right PICC, ending in the low SVC.   

The thoracic aorta is unremarkable aside from scattered calcifications.  A
9-mm partially calcified hyperdensity situated between the takeoff of the
brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery is likely a lymph node
(2:14), unchanged in appearance compared to CT from ___.  The
heart is grossly unremarkable.  There is no pericardial effusion.  No
pathologically enlarged hilar or axillary lymph nodes are seen.

There is mild biapical pleural parenchymal scarring/thickening as well as mild
centrilobular emphysema.  A small left pleural effusion is increased compared
to CT from ___, while a trace right pleural effusion is not
significantly changed.  There is mild bilateral dependent atelectasis.  The
airways are patent to the subsegmental levels bilaterally.

This study was not optimized for evaluation of the abdominal contents.  Note
is made of a 9-mm gallstone within the body of the gallbladder, as before.  An
11-mm simple cyst is seen within the right interpolar region. There is a
moderate to high grade stenosis of the celiac origin.

BONE WINDOW:  The patient is status post midline sternotomy.  No suspicious
lytic or blastic lesions are identified.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Marked interval improvement in degree of esophageal wall thickening and
periesophageal fat stranding, consistent with improving esophagitis.

2.  Increased left small pleural effusion and unchanged right trace pleural
effusion.

3.  Cholelithiasis.

4.  Chronic, moderate to high grade stenosis of the celiac origin.

INDICATION:  ___ man with malfunctioning PICC.  Evaluate for clot.

COMPARISON:  No relevant comparisons available.

FINDINGS:

Grayscale and Doppler images of the right and left subclavian, right axillary,
basilic, brachial, and cephalic vein were obtained.  There is wall-to-wall
flow with normal compression and augmentation in all visible veins. 
Incidental note is made of duplicated brachial vein system (4 total brachial
veins).  A PICC line is noted in the right basilic vein.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence DVT in the right upper extremity.
